A long-hafted axe needed room to swing and recover in foot combat. Shaft, edge and grip affected use, while comrades, narrow ground and shields constrained movement. Damaged handles and loose fittings needed skilled repair. Fighters needed room to wield or shoot without harming comrades. Spares and repair access mattered more to continued service than boasts of defeating armor in one blow.

Requisitioned craftsmen left other work, and issued weapons still needed trained users.
